text:
jordan: Customer (acme-prod) opened ticket #CS-9982 — after upgrading the TS/Node SDK to v0.22.0 they're getting 404s for chat route. They say code used to work on v0.21.x.

sam: Can you paste the snippet they're calling and the exact error body?

jordan: Pasted below from their log (sanitized):
```json
{
  "status":404,
  "error":"Not Found",
  "path":"/v1/chat.create"
}
```
They call `client.chat.create({ model: 'gpt-4a', messages })`.

ingrid: Hmm we renamed some endpoints in API v1. New route is `/v1/chat/sessions.create` and SDK should map but maybe client-side mapping changed. Which SDK package exactly are they on?

jordan: @sam they reported `@redwood/sdk` @ `0.22.0`. They said v0.21.4 worked.

elena: I think 0.22.0 introduced the route name change and parameter rename (`sessionId` -> `conversationId`) in the client surface. Could be both route + param mismatch.

sam: Requesting repro steps from customer: Node version, exact SDK import, minimal repro. Could we reproduce quickly on our side by installing 0.22.0?

jordan: They already provided a repro gist: https://gist.github.com/acme/repro-cc (sanitized). Minimal snippet:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'gpt-4a', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] });
```

dev-bot: New support severity set to P2 — multiple timeouts/404s reported by customer.

ingrid: I spun up a sandbox and installed `@redwood/sdk@0.22.0` — confirmed `client.chat.create` now throws 404. The SDK in 0.22 expects `client.chat.session.create` shape. Looks like a breaking surface change that wasn't in the compatibility notes.

elena: Two immediate options: 1) advise customer to pin `@redwood/sdk@0.21.4` (workaround) OR 2) server-side route alias to accept `/v1/chat.create` and map to new handler. Which do we want to push?

jordan: Customer wants a quick fix (they're in prod). They prefer no code changes. Can ops add a temporary alias for `/v1/chat.create`?

oncall-eng: ops can add an internal redirect for legacy route for a short window, but need ENG signoff that payload compatibility is safe (param names). If SDK changed param names too we need to confirm mapping rules.

sam: I can open an eng ticket. Repro notes: 0.21.4 -> works; 0.22.0 -> 404. Attach sandbox logs and stack traces.

elena: Confirmed parameter mapping: older SDK used `chat.create({ messages })`. New SDK surface uses `chat.sessions.create({ conversationId?, messages })`. We can implement route alias that accepts old shape and maps `messages` -> `messages` and leaves conversationId undefined. Should be safe for most calls.

ingrid: Also found a docs failure — changelog didn't mention breaking rename. Need a docs/compat note and publish patch to SDK that reintroduces backwards-compatible wrapper.

sam: Action items:
- sam -> create ENG issue with repro, tag eng-runtime and devex (ETA 24h)
- oncall-eng -> provision temporary /v1/chat.create alias (ops ticket) and monitor errors
- jordan -> reply to customer with workaround (pin to 0.21.4) and ETA for server-side alias
- elena -> draft SDK patch that re-adds `client.chat.create` forwarding and publish 0.22.1 if possible

jordan: I'll message customer with pinned workaround and ask permission to enable a transient alias.

oncall-eng: Alias created internally: route /v1/chat.create -> /internal/mapping/chat/sessions.create (starting in 10m). Monitoring: set retention to 1h and alert on >1% 5xx rate.

dev-bot: Deploy success — alias live.

jordan: Customer confirmed alias removed 404s but reported a 1-2s added latency. They accepted workaround and will hold off upgrading SDK until patch.

elena: I'll cut a quick 0.22.1 with compatibility shim and a deprecation warning in console. Also update changelog.

sam: @eng-runtime please review the proposed shim: `client.chat.create = (...args) => client.chat.sessions.create(...args)` and ensure telemetry/events still surface correctly.

ingrid: Noted. We'll also add an integration test to prevent this regression.

jordan: Thanks team — I'll close the support ticket once 0.22.1 is published and customer verifies. :thumbsup:
